title: Implement a real headless agent adapter with isolated role sessions
objective: Replace manual role packet copy and paste with fresh automated provider sessions through Vibez’s neutral runner and unchanged owning gates.
inScope: Implement one documented provider with host-owned capability enforcement and narrow read/write tools. Keep provider/model binaries and credentials outside the repository.
Persist invocation and session identity, redacted public metadata and durable restart handling. Reject stale results and preserve source revision changes across developer handoff.
Exercise actual independent isolated Developer, QA, Architect and UAT/Product sessions and all documented failure paths.
outOfScope: Vendor dependencies in the neutral engine, unrestricted shell or network, GUI automation, AUT-003 scheduling or policy replacement, package release.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-01: At least one real provider runs all configured required roles without copying packets/results or manually switching chats.
AC-02: Every role has fresh scoped context and enforced tool permissions; Developer cannot self-approve via labels or shared session state.
AC-03: Returned results validate through the unchanged owning gates; malformed/wrong-binding output cannot advance lifecycle.
AC-04: Restart/uncertain dispatch reconciles the original session or blocks safely, without duplicate active writers.
AC-05: Cancellation/timeout and budget enforcement are honest about external work still running.
AC-06: Manual-provider compatibility and a documented neutral conformance contract remain intact.
validationPlan: Run all README checks, conformance and independent role reviews.
Exercise wrong/stale bindings, malformed output, transport failure, timed-out or cancelled workers, resource/cost refusal and lost acknowledgement without duplicate workers.

Run a fresh actual provider task in an isolated disposable checkout with developer source change, deterministic validation and three independent review contexts entering the native gates. Confirm manual fallback and rollback from a stopped set of sessions.
